title: Propositional interpolation from cut-free proofs

based_on.title: Interpolation through the Lens of Proof Theory (corrected December 2025 version)
based_on.pages: Section 2.3 and Figures 2.3–2.4 pp. 6–8; section 3.2 pp. 12–16, Lemma 3.12 and Figure 3.2. Use corrected Dec 2025 file.

summary: Extract an interpolant and two factor proofs recursively from a cut-free propositional tree, with an exact common-atom bound.
abstract: A proof of an implication may mention atoms that occur only on one side. An interpolant expresses the part of the argument that can be stated using only the atom names shared by the premise and conclusion. We construct such a formula directly from a finite sequent proof, returning two proof certificates that factor the original argument. Each rule determines how the smaller interpolants are combined, while the common-atom bound is preserved at every step. Cut removal makes the construction available to proofs with intermediate lemmas, and analytic search connects it to ordinary classical deductions with numbered atoms. Worked examples show why the middle formula can be a constant and why the conditions do not make it unique.
